model.title: PEACE in Sudan Act
model.meta: Foreign Relations Committee · Sen. James Risch (R-ID)

summary.text: The bill would state that it is US policy to end the war in Sudan, hold those responsible for atrocities accountable, and protect the human rights of Sudanese people. It would require the State Department to report regularly to Congress on foreign governments and armed groups fueling the conflict, on human rights abuses, and on the financial assets and business interests tied to the fighting. It would direct the Secretary of State to develop a strategy for a ceasefire and political settlement, and to assess whether armed groups in Sudan should be designated as specially designated global terrorists. It would allow the President to impose sanctions, including asset blocking and visa bans, on people responsible for the violence, with exceptions for humanitarian aid. It would also limit US support for Sudan's government at international financial institutions and in foreign assistance, extend the Special Envoy for Sudan's term, and require an updated business risk advisory. The requirements would end once a durable peace is certified, and the Act would expire five years after enactment.
